title: Home & neighbourhood
goal: Rent a flat in Bengaluru, deal with the owner about the deposit, rent and bills, report what is broken, get it fixed, and complain to neighbours without starting a war.
intro:
Renting in Bengaluru has its own vocabulary, and most of it is English said the Kannada way: the **ಓನರ್**, the **ಅಡ್ವಾನ್ಸ್** (deposit), the **ಅಗ್ರಿಮೆಂಟ್**, the **ಮೇಂಟೆನೆನ್ಸ್**. What holds it together is Kannada grammar: *what* is broken, *since when*, and *who is going to get it fixed*.

This unit gives you three tools. First, how to say what's wrong (ಕೆಟ್ಟು ಹೋಗಿದೆ 'it's broken', ಮೂರು ದಿನದಿಂದ ಸೋರ್ತಿದೆ 'it's been leaking for three days'). Second, how to ask and complain politely but firmly. Third, the **causative** ಮಾಡಿಸು 'get it done', the verb every tenant needs: ಯಾವಾಗ ಸರಿ ಮಾಡಿಸ್ತೀರಾ? 'When will you get it fixed?'

vocab.note: Formal ಮಾಲೀಕ mālīka / ಮನೆ ಮಾಲೀಕ. Tenants usually address the owner as ಅಂಕಲ್ / ಆಂಟಿ, or ಸಾರ್ / ಮೇಡಂ.
Usually charges one month's rent as commission.
Bengaluru deposits are famously large: traditionally ten months' rent, now often three to six. Refunded when you leave, minus painting and repairs.
Formal ಒಪ್ಪಂದ oppanda or ಕರಾರು karāru. Usually for 11 months, on stamp paper.
Means the whole building. Your own flat is just ಮನೆ (or ಫ್ಲ್ಯಾಟ್).

vocab.en: maintenance charge (monthly fee in an apartment)
vocab.note: Paid to the residents' association for the watchman, lift, water and cleaning.
ಖಾಲಿ ಇದೆ 'it's vacant'; ಮನೆ ಖಾಲಿ ಮಾಡು 'to vacate the house, move out'.
Also the English ಟ್ಯಾಪ್. Don't confuse with the ending -ನಲ್ಲಿ 'in'.
Spoken continuous ಸೋರ್ತಿದೆ 'is leaking'. A leak is ಸೋರಿಕೆ.
Said 'fyān'. Switch it on: ಫ್ಯಾನ್ ಹಾಕು; off: ಫ್ಯಾನ್ ಆಫ್ ಮಾಡು.
ಕರೆಂಟ್ ಹೋಯ್ತು 'the power went', ಕರೆಂಟ್ ಬಂತು 'it's back'. Formal ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ vidyut.
Every Bengaluru bathroom has one. ಗೀಸರ್ ಹಾಕು 'switch on the geyser'; wait ten minutes before your bath.
ಗಾಜಿನ ಲೋಟ 'a glass tumbler', ಕಿಟಕಿ ಗಾಜು 'window pane'.
Lit. 'make right'. Same meaning as ರಿಪೇರಿ ಮಾಡು. Causative: ಸರಿ ಮಾಡಿಸು 'get it fixed'.

vocab.en: to get (something) put in, fitted, installed
vocab.note: Causative of ಹಾಕು 'put'. ಹೊಸ ಬೀಗ ಹಾಕಿಸು 'get a new lock fitted', ಫ್ಯಾನ್ ಹಾಕಿಸು 'get a fan installed'.
ಲಿಫ್ಟ್ ಕೆಟ್ಟು ಹೋಗಿದೆ 'the lift is out of order'. During power cuts it runs on the building's generator, if at all.
Lit. 'the work people'. ಕೆಲಸದವಳು (f) is common but blunter; many families call her ಅಕ್ಕ or by name.

vocab.en: to pay (rent, a bill, a fee); to tie; to build
vocab.note: Past ಕಟ್ಟಿದ-. ಬಾಡಿಗೆ ಕಟ್ಟು 'pay the rent', ಬಿಲ್ ಕಟ್ಟು 'pay a bill'. Paying a shopkeeper is just ಕೊಡು.
ಕರೆಂಟ್ ಬಿಲ್ (from BESCOM), ನೀರಿನ ಬಿಲ್ (from BWSSB).

vocab.en: outstanding, still due; the rest, remaining
vocab.note: ಬಾಡಿಗೆ ಬಾಕಿ ಇದೆ 'the rent is still due'; ಬಾಕಿ ಕೆಲಸ 'the remaining work'.
Ordered when piped Cauvery water or the borewell runs short, especially in summer.
In everyday talk: ಪಕ್ಕದ ಮನೆಯವರು 'the people next door', ಮೇಲಿನ ಮನೆಯವರು 'the people upstairs'.
ಸದ್ದು ಮಾಡಬೇಡ 'don't make a sound'. ಗಲಾಟೆ is noise made by people; ಸದ್ದು is any sound, a drip, a bang, a drill. For music and TV volume everyone says ಸೌಂಡ್.
From ಜೋರು 'force, loudness'. ಮಳೆ ಜೋರಾಗಿ ಬರ್ತಿದೆ 'it's raining hard'.

vocab.en: to tolerate, put up with, bear
vocab.note: Mostly in the negative: ಸಹಿಸೋಕೆ ಆಗಲ್ಲ 'I can't stand it'.
Also ಸೆಕ್ಯುರಿಟಿ. Usually addressed as ಅಣ್ಣ.
The person who collects maintenance and hears complaints. Formal ಕಾರ್ಯದರ್ಶಿ.
ಮನೆ ಶಿಫ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡು 'to move house / move your things'; ಶಿಫ್ಟ್ ಆಗು 'to move (yourself)'.
A puja and a meal when you move into a new house you own; friends bring a gift.

phrases.note: Look for the board ಮನೆ ಬಾಡಿಗೆಗೆ ಇದೆ / TO-LET on the gate.

phrases.en: How much deposit do I have to pay?
Is maintenance included in the rent?
The tap in the bathroom is leaking.
Please don't mind, there's something I needed to tell you.
phrases.note: The standard soft opening for a complaint. Careful form: ಬೇಜಾರು ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಬೇಡಿ.

phrases.en: When will you get it fixed? (polite)
Could you turn the sound down a bit? (polite)
phrases.note: ಸೌಂಡ್ 'sound, volume' is what everyone says for music or TV.

phrases.en: How many times do I have to say it?
phrases.note: Exasperated. Careful form: ಎಷ್ಟು ಸಲ ಹೇಳುವುದು?

phrases.native: ನಾವು ಮುಂದಿನ ತಿಂಗಳು ಮನೆ ಖಾಲಿ ಮಾಡ್ತೀವಿ
phrases.roman: nāvu mundina tiṅgaḷu mane khāli māḍtīvi

phrases.en: When will you return the deposit?

grammar.title: Saying what's wrong: -ಇ ಹೋಗಿದೆ, the continuous, and -ಇಂದ 'for / since'
grammar.body:
Three patterns cover almost every complaint about a house.

**1. Something broke: past participle + ಹೋಗು.** Kannada adds ಹೋಗು 'go' to a verb of breaking or spoiling, the way English says 'it's gone off' or 'it's gone missing'. The present perfect **ಹೋಗಿದೆ** says it *is* broken now; the past **ಹೋಯ್ತು** tells the moment it happened:
ಕೆಡು → ಕೆಟ್ಟು ಹೋಗಿದೆ 'has broken down' (machines, food)
ಒಡೆ → ಒಡೆದು ಹೋಗಿದೆ 'has cracked / smashed' (glass, pipes)
ಮುರಿ → ಮುರಿದು ಹೋಗಿದೆ 'has snapped' (a chair leg, a handle)
ಕಳೆ → ಕಳೆದು ಹೋಯ್ತು 'got lost'
Without ಹೋಗು the sentence has a doer and sounds deliberate: ಅವನು ಗಾಜು ಒಡೆದ 'he broke the glass'.

**2. A fault that keeps going: the continuous.** ಸೋರ್ತಿದೆ 'is leaking', ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡ್ತಿಲ್ಲ 'isn't working', ನೀರು ಬರ್ತಿಲ್ಲ 'no water is coming'. Power and water *go* and *come*: ಕರೆಂಟ್ ಹೋಗಿದೆ 'the power's out', ಕರೆಂಟ್ ಬಂತು 'the power's back'.

**3. How long: -ಇಂದ.** The 'from' ending on a time word means 'since' or 'for (up to now)': ನಿನ್ನೆಯಿಂದ 'since yesterday', ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆಯಿಂದ 'since morning', ಮೂರು ದಿನದಿಂದ 'for three days', ಒಂದು ವಾರದಿಂದ 'for a week'. Where English switches to 'has been leaking', Kannada keeps the plain continuous: ಮೂರು ದಿನದಿಂದ ಸೋರ್ತಿದೆ 'it's been leaking for three days'.

The trap is the dative: ಮೂರು ದಿನಕ್ಕೆ means 'for three days' in the sense of a planned period (a room for three days), not 'for the last three days'.

examples.native: ಗೀಸರ್ ಕೆಟ್ಟು ಹೋಗಿದೆ, ಬಿಸಿ ನೀರು ಇಲ್ಲ.
examples.roman: gīsar keṭṭu hōgide, bisi nīru illa.
examples.en: The geyser's broken, there's no hot water.
The leg of the chair has snapped.
There's been no water since this morning.
The lift hasn't been working for two weeks.

grammar.title: Requests and complaints: softening and insisting
grammar.body:
With an owner, a neighbour or the apartment secretary you want to be firm without being rude. Kannada does it with a handful of forms, from softest to firmest.

**Softest, 'would it be possible?'**: infinitive (spoken **-ಓಕೆ**, written -ಅಲು) + **ಆಗುತ್ತಾ?**: ಇವತ್ತು ಬರೋಕೆ ಆಗುತ್ತಾ? 'would you be able to come today?' (written ಬರಲು ಆಗುತ್ತದೆಯೇ?). The answer 'can't' is ಆಗಲ್ಲ: ಇವತ್ತು ಆಗಲ್ಲ, ನಾಳೆ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ.

**Polite, 'will you?'**: ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ + the future as a question in **-ತೀರಾ?**: ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ನೋಡ್ತೀರಾ? 'could you have a look?'. ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ 'a little' takes the edge off any request, like English 'just'.

**Opening gently, -ಬೇಕಿತ್ತು**: the past of ಬೇಕು means 'I needed / I was meaning to': ಒಂದು ವಿಷಯ ಹೇಳಬೇಕಿತ್ತು 'there's something I wanted to tell you', ನಿಮ್ಮ ಹತ್ರ ಮಾತಾಡಬೇಕಿತ್ತು 'I wanted a word with you'. Put ಬೇಜಾರು ಮಾಡ್ಕೋಬೇಡಿ 'please don't mind' in front and the complaint lands softly.

**Asking someone to stop**: a plain ಮಾಡಬೇಡಿ 'please don't' is fine, but between neighbours it's gentler to say what *would be good*: negative 'if' (-ಅದಿದ್ರೆ) + **ಒಳ್ಳೇದು**: ಹಾಕದಿದ್ರೆ ಒಳ್ಳೇದು 'it'd be good if you didn't put it on'.

**Insisting**: the emphatic **-ಏ** pins down a time: **ಇವತ್ತೇ** 'today itself', **ಈಗಲೇ** 'right now', ಈ ವಾರದಲ್ಲೇ 'this week, no later'. ಎಷ್ಟು ಸಲ ಹೇಳೋದು? 'how many times do I have to say it?' and ಮೂರು ಸಲ ಹೇಳಿದ್ದೀನಿ 'I've told you three times' show your patience has run out. Stay with **ನೀವು** even when annoyed: dropping to ನೀನು with an adult you don't know is an insult and turns a complaint into a fight.

examples.en: Would it be possible to get it fixed a bit sooner?
Madam, I wanted a quick word with you.

examples.native: ನಿಮ್ಮ ಕಾರು ನಮ್ಮ ಗೇಟ್ ಮುಂದೆ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಬೇಡಿ.
examples.roman: nimma kāru namma gēṭ munde nillisabēḍi.
examples.en: Please don't park your car in front of our gate.

examples.native: ರಾತ್ರಿ ಹತ್ತರ ನಂತರ ಮ್ಯೂಸಿಕ್ ಹಾಕದಿದ್ರೆ ಒಳ್ಳೇದು.
examples.roman: rātri hattara nantara myūsik hākadidre oḷḷēdu.
examples.en: It'd be good if you didn't play music after ten at night.
I've told you three times, he has to come today.

grammar.title: Causatives revisited: getting it done, and by whom
grammar.body:
A causative verb means 'have / get / make someone do it'. You met it in unit 25 for errands; at home it's the verb that decides who actually turns up with the spanner. You build it by adding **-ಇಸು** to the verb stem:
ಮಾಡು → **ಮಾಡಿಸು** 'get (something) done'
ಹಾಕು → **ಹಾಕಿಸು** 'get (something) put in, installed'
ತರು → **ತರಿಸು** 'have (something) brought, order in'
ಕರೆ → **ಕರೆಸು** 'send for, call (someone) in'
ತೊಳೆ → **ತೊಳೆಸು** 'get (something) washed'
ಬರೆ → **ಬರೆಸು** 'get (something) written'
ನಿಲ್ಲು → **ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸು** 'stop (something), park'

The result is an ordinary verb in -ಉ, so every tense works: ಮಾಡಿಸ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll get it done', ಮಾಡಿಸಿದೆ 'I got it done', ಮಾಡಿಸಿದ್ದಾರೆ 'they've had it done', ಮಾಡಿಸಿಲ್ಲ 'hasn't had it done', ಮಾಡಿಸ್ಬೇಕು 'need to get it done', ಮಾಡಿಸೋಕೆ ಆಗುತ್ತಾ? 'can you get it done?'.

**The person who does the work** takes **ಕೈಲಿ** (written ಕೈಯಲ್ಲಿ, 'in the hand of'): ಪ್ಲಂಬರ್ ಕೈಲಿ ಮಾಡಿಸಿ 'get the plumber to do it'. Someone you *send for* takes the object ending: ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಿಷಿಯನ್‌ನ ಕರೆಸಿ 'call in the electrician'.

**For yourself or for someone else**: add ಕೊಳ್ಳು when it's for your own benefit (ಮಾಡಿಸ್ಕೊಂಡೆ 'I got it done (for myself)') and ಕೊಡು when it's a favour to someone (ಮಾಡಿಸ್ಕೊಡಿ 'please get it done for me', the tenant's favourite request).

**The trap**: the plain verb means you do it with your own hands. ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಿ ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll fix the tap (myself)' vs ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಿ ಮಾಡಿಸ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll get the tap fixed'. An owner who says the first is promising to turn up with his own spanner.

examples.en: Please get a new lock put on the door for me.
The owner has had the house painted.
No cooking today, let's order food in.

examples.native: ಅಮ್ಮ ಕೆಲಸದವರ ಕೈಲಿ ಮನೆ ಕ್ಲೀನ್ ಮಾಡಿಸ್ತಾರೆ.
examples.roman: amma kelasadavara kaili mane klīn māḍistāre.
examples.en: Mum gets the help to clean the house.
You still haven't got the tap fixed?

dialogue.title: Calling the owner
dialogue.setting: Ananya rents a flat in HSR Layout. The bathroom tap has been dripping for a week, so she calls the owner, Murthy uncle, who lives in Jayanagar.

lines.native: ಹಲೋ, ಮೂರ್ತಿ ಅಂಕಲ್? ನಾನು ಅನನ್ಯ, ಮೂರನೇ ಮಹಡಿ.
lines.roman: halō, mūrti aṅkal? nānu ananya, mūranē mahaḍi.
lines.en: Hello, Murthy uncle? It's Ananya, third floor.
Yes, tell me, dear. What's up?

lines.native: ಬೇಜಾರು ಮಾಡ್ಕೋಬೇಡಿ ಅಂಕಲ್, ಬಾತ್‌ರೂಮಲ್ಲಿ ನಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದು ವಾರದಿಂದ ಸೋರ್ತಿದೆ.
lines.roman: bējāru māḍkōbēḍi aṅkal, bātrūmalli nalli ondu vāradinda sōrtide.
lines.en: Sorry to bother you, uncle, the bathroom tap has been leaking for a week.

lines.native: ಅಯ್ಯೋ, ಹೌದಾ? ಹೋದ ತಿಂಗಳು ತಾನೇ ಸರಿ ಮಾಡಿಸಿದ್ದೆ.
lines.roman: ayyō, haudā? hōda tiṅgaḷu tānē sari māḍisidde.
lines.en: Oh no, really? I only got it fixed last month.

lines.native: ಹೌದು, ಆದ್ರೆ ಮತ್ತೆ ಶುರುವಾಗಿದೆ. ರಾತ್ರಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಟಪ್ ಟಪ್ ಅಂತ ಸದ್ದು, ನಿದ್ದೆನೇ ಬರಲ್ಲ.
lines.roman: haudu, ādre matte shuruvāgide. rātri ellā ṭap ṭap anta saddu, niddenē baralla.
lines.en: Yes, but it's started again. Drip, drip all night, I can't sleep at all.

lines.native: ಸರಿ ಸರಿ. ನಮ್ಮ ಪ್ಲಂಬರ್ ಕೈಲಿ ನಾಳೆ ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ಮಾಡಿಸ್ತೀನಿ.
lines.roman: sari sari. namma plambar kaili nāḷe beḷigge māḍistīni.
lines.en: OK, OK. I'll get our plumber to do it tomorrow morning.

lines.native: ನಾಳೆ ನಾನು ಆಫೀಸಲ್ಲಿ ಇರ್ತೀನಿ... ಇವತ್ತು ಸಂಜೆನೇ ಕಳಿಸೋಕೆ ಆಗುತ್ತಾ?
lines.roman: nāḷe nānu āphīsalli irtīni... ivattu sañjenē kaḷisōke āguttā?
lines.en: Tomorrow I'll be at the office... would it be possible to send him this evening?

lines.native: ನೋಡ್ತೀನಿ, ಅವನಿಗೆ ಫೋನ್ ಮಾಡಿ ಹೇಳ್ತೀನಿ. ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ವಿಷಯ, ಈ ತಿಂಗಳ ಮೇಂಟೆನೆನ್ಸ್ ಕಟ್ಟಿದ್ಯಾ?
lines.roman: nōḍtīni, avanige phōn māḍi hēḷtīni. innondu viṣaya, ī tiṅgaḷa mēṇṭenens kaṭṭidyā?
lines.en: I'll see, I'll call him and tell him. One more thing, have you paid this month's maintenance?

lines.native: ಕಟ್ಟಿದ್ದೀನಿ ಅಂಕಲ್, ಸೆಕ್ರೆಟರಿಗೆ ಕೊಟ್ಟೆ. ಆಮೇಲೆ... ಪಕ್ಕದ ಮನೆಯವರು ರಾತ್ರಿ ಹನ್ನೆರಡರವರೆಗೂ ಜೋರಾಗಿ ಮ್ಯೂಸಿಕ್ ಹಾಕ್ತಾರೆ.
lines.roman: kaṭṭiddīni aṅkal, sekreṭarige koṭṭe. āmēle... pakkada maneyavaru rātri hanneraḍaravaregū jōrāgi myūsik hāktāre.
lines.en: I've paid it, uncle, I gave it to the secretary. And also... the people next door play loud music till midnight.

lines.native: ಹೌದಾ? ಅವರು ಹೊಸಬರು. ಒಂದು ಸಲ ಸೌಂಡ್ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳು, ಕೇಳ್ತಾರೆ.
lines.roman: haudā? avaru hosabaru. ondu sala sauṇḍ kaḍime māḍi anta hēḷu, kēḷtāre.
lines.en: Really? They're new. Just ask them once to turn it down, they'll listen.

lines.native: ಎರಡು ಸಲ ಹೇಳಿದ್ದೀನಿ ಅಂಕಲ್! ಏನೂ ಪ್ರಯೋಜನ ಇಲ್ಲ.
lines.roman: eraḍu sala hēḷiddīni aṅkal! ēnū prayōjana illa.
lines.en: I've told them twice, uncle! It's no use.

lines.native: ಸರಿ, ಹಾಗಾದ್ರೆ ನಾನೇ ಮಾತಾಡ್ತೀನಿ. ನೀನು ಚಿಂತೆ ಮಾಡ್ಬೇಡ.
lines.roman: sari, hāgādre nānē mātāḍtīni. nīnu chinte māḍbēḍa.
lines.en: Fine, then I'll talk to them myself. Don't you worry.

lines.native: ತುಂಬಾ ಥ್ಯಾಂಕ್ಸ್ ಅಂಕಲ್. ಪ್ಲಂಬರ್ ಬರೋ ಮುಂಚೆ ಒಂದು ಮೆಸೇಜ್ ಹಾಕಿ.
lines.roman: tumbā thyāṅks aṅkal. plambar barō muñche ondu mesēj hāki.
lines.en: Thanks a lot, uncle. Drop me a message before the plumber comes.

culture:
Renting in Bengaluru runs on a few unwritten rules. The **ಅಡ್ವಾನ್ಸ್** is big (traditionally ten months' rent, now more often three to six), the **ಅಗ್ರಿಮೆಂಟ್** is for eleven months on stamp paper, and when you leave the owner usually keeps a month's rent or so for painting. Some owners still ask whether you're vegetarian or 'family' (not bachelors), and many live upstairs or next door, so the relationship is personal: tenants call them **ಅಂಕಲ್ / ಆಂಟಿ**, and they often reply in the informal ನೀನು with -ಅಮ್ಮ or -ಪ್ಪ (ಹೇಳಮ್ಮ, ಬಾರಪ್ಪ), which is affectionate, not rude. You still answer with ನೀವು.

Complaints start soft (ಬೇಜಾರು ಮಾಡ್ಕೋಬೇಡಿ..., ಒಂದು ವಿಷಯ ಹೇಳಬೇಕಿತ್ತು) and escalate slowly; going straight to the residents' association or raising your voice makes you 'that tenant'. Daily life has its own vocabulary: the BBMP **ಕಸದ ಗಾಡಿ** comes early and wants wet and dry waste separated, the **ಕರೆಂಟ್ ಬಿಲ್** comes from BESCOM, and in April and May whole apartment blocks depend on the **ಟ್ಯಾಂಕರ್**. When people buy a home they hold a **ಗೃಹಪ್ರವೇಶ**: a morning puja, a big banana-leaf lunch, and an invitation it's rude to skip.

tip.title: Broken: ಕೆಟ್ಟು ಹೋಗಿದೆ · since: -ಇಂದ
tip.body:
- Broke: past participle + **ಹೋಗಿದೆ**: **ಕೆಟ್ಟು** ಹೋಗಿದೆ 'has broken down', **ಒಡೆದು** ಹೋಗಿದೆ 'is cracked'.
- Still going on: the continuous: **ಸೋರ್ತಿದೆ** 'is leaking', ಕೆಲಸ **ಮಾಡ್ತಿಲ್ಲ** 'isn't working'.
- How long: time word + **-ಇಂದ**: ನಿನ್ನೆ**ಯಿಂದ**, ಮೂರು ದಿನ**ದಿಂದ** 'for three days'. Not -ಗೆ.

sentences.en: The kitchen tap has been leaking for two days.
The fan's broken down.
The window pane is cracked.
No power since last night.
The water hasn't been coming properly for a week.

sentences.native: ಮಗು ಆಡುವಾಗ ಗಾಜಿನ ಲೋಟ ಒಡೆದು ಹೋಯ್ತು.
sentences.roman: magu āḍuvāga gājina lōṭa oḍedu hōytu.
sentences.en: The glass tumbler broke while the kid was playing.

sentences.native: ಫ್ಯಾನ್ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡ್ತಿಲ್ಲ, ತುಂಬಾ ಸೆಕೆ ಆಗ್ತಿದೆ.
sentences.roman: phyān kelasa māḍtilla, tumbā seke āgtide.
sentences.en: The fan isn't working and it's really stuffy.

sentences.native: ಗೀಸರ್ ಹಾಕಿ ಅರ್ಧ ಗಂಟೆ ಆಯ್ತು, ಇನ್ನೂ ಬಿಸಿ ನೀರು ಬಂದಿಲ್ಲ.
sentences.roman: gīsar hāki ardha gaṇṭe āytu, innū bisi nīru bandilla.
sentences.en: The geyser's been on for half an hour and there's still no hot water.
When will the power come back?

sentences.native: ಬಾತ್‌ರೂಮಲ್ಲಿ ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸೋರಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಒದ್ದೆ ಆಗಿದೆ.
sentences.roman: bātrūmalli nalli sōri ellā odde āgide.
sentences.en: The tap in the bathroom leaked and everything's wet.

tip.title: Softening and insisting
tip.body:
- Polite: **ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ** + verb + **-ತೀರಾ?**: ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ನೋಡ್ತೀರಾ? 'could you take a look?'
- Softer: **-ಓಕೆ ಆಗುತ್ತಾ?**: ಇವತ್ತು ಬರೋಕೆ ಆಗುತ್ತಾ? 'would it be possible to come today?'
- Opening gently: **-ಬೇಕಿತ್ತು** 'I wanted to': ಒಂದು ವಿಷಯ ಹೇಳಬೇಕಿತ್ತು.
- Insisting: **-ಏ**: ಇವತ್ತೇ 'today itself', ಈಗಲೇ 'right now'. Keep ನೀವು even when annoyed.

sentences.en: Could you come and take a look, sir?
Would it be possible to send the plumber today itself?
Sir, there was something I wanted to ask.
Please fix it this week itself.
We need an electrician to fix the fan.

sentences.native: ನಿಮಗೆ ಸಮಯ ಇಲ್ಲ ಅಂದ್ರೆ ನಾನೇ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಿಷಿಯನ್‌ನ ಕರೀಲಾ?
sentences.roman: nimage samaya illa andre nānē elekṭrishiyanna karīlā?
sentences.en: If you don't have time, shall I call an electrician myself?

sentences.native: ಬೇಜಾರು ಮಾಡ್ಕೋಬೇಡಿ, ಈ ತಿಂಗಳು ಬಾಡಿಗೆ ಎರಡು ದಿನ ತಡ ಆಗುತ್ತೆ.
sentences.roman: bējāru māḍkōbēḍi, ī tiṅgaḷu bāḍige eraḍu dina taḍa āgutte.
sentences.en: Please don't mind, the rent will be two days late this month.

No matter how often I say it, nobody's come.

tip.title: Get it done: ಮಾಡಿಸು
tip.body:
- Causative = stem + **-ಇಸು**: ಮಾಡು → **ಮಾಡಿಸು**, ಹಾಕು → **ಹಾಕಿಸು**, ತೊಳೆ → **ತೊಳೆಸು**, ಬರೆ → **ಬರೆಸು**.
- Normal tenses: **ಮಾಡಿಸ್ತೀನಿ** 'I'll get it done', **ಮಾಡಿಸಿದ್ರಾ?** 'did you get it done?', **ಮಾಡಿಸಿಲ್ಲ** 'hasn't'.
- The worker takes **ಕೈಲಿ**: ಪ್ಲಂಬರ್ ಕೈಲಿ ಮಾಡಿಸಿ.
- Trap: ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ = I'll do it myself.

sentences.native: ನಾಳೆ ಪ್ಲಂಬರ್ ಕೈಲಿ ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಿ ಮಾಡಿಸ್ತೀನಿ.
sentences.roman: nāḷe plambar kaili nalli sari māḍistīni.
sentences.en: I'll get the plumber to fix the tap tomorrow.

sentences.native: ಬೀಗ ಕೆಟ್ಟು ಹೋಗಿದೆ, ಹೊಸ ಬೀಗ ಹಾಕಿಸಿ.
sentences.roman: bīga keṭṭu hōgide, hosa bīga hākisi.

sentences.native: ನಾಳೆ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಿಷಿಯನ್‌ನ ಕರೆಸಿ ಹೊಸ ಫ್ಯಾನ್ ಹಾಕಿಸ್ತೀನಿ.

sentences.native: ಲಿಫ್ಟ್ ಕೆಟ್ಟು ಹೋಗಿದೆ, ಯಾರೂ ರಿಪೇರಿ ಮಾಡಿಸಿಲ್ಲ.

sentences.native: ಈ ತಿಂಗಳ ಬಾಡಿಗೆ ಕಟ್ಟಿದ್ದೀನಿ, ಬಾಕಿ ಏನೂ ಇಲ್ಲ.
sentences.roman: ī tiṅgaḷa bāḍige kaṭṭiddīni, bāki ēnū illa.

sentences.roman: namma nerehore tumbā chennāgide, ellarū sahāya māḍtāre.

lessons.title: Moving out, moving in
new: ನಾವು ಮುಂದಿನ ತಿಂಗಳು ಮನೆ ಖಾಲಿ ಮಾಡ್ತೀವಿ

sentences.native: ಸಾಮಾನು ಶಿಫ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡೋಕೆ ಎರಡು ದಿನ ಬೇಕು.
sentences.roman: sāmānu shifṭ māḍōke eraḍu dina bēku.

sentences.native: ಮನೆ ಖಾಲಿ ಮಾಡೋಕೆ ಒಂದು ತಿಂಗಳು ಮುಂಚೆ ಓನರ್‌ಗೆ ಹೇಳಬೇಕು.
